name: Rate Limiter
description: Sliding-window rate limiter + tenant-plan-based quota enforcement (seat/feature/usage limits).

permissions.name: View the installation's rate limits and bans
permissions.description: Root tenant only. The sign-in limits, address bans and anonymous API limit of the whole installation.

permissions.name: Change the installation's rate limits and bans
permissions.description: Root tenant only. Each limit can only be made stricter than the built-in value.

permissions.name: Ban and unban addresses for the whole installation
permissions.description: Root tenant only. Ban an address or CIDR block from every page and API of the installation for a while, with a reason, and lift a ban. Every ban and lift is audited.

extensions.description: Phase 55 00 §0.7: every minute, publishes the standing long address bans for the node's edge (Redis edge:app-bans, which infra/compose/edge/fleet-edge-sync turns into CrowdSec local decisions) and reports the local CrowdSec decisions the host handed back as edge.decision rows.

metadata.label: Stop counting a revoked session as its person

extensions.description: Phase 55 01.6: the signal kinds this module emits (the audit actions it owns), each attribute with its personal-data class. Read by ai_firewall through its registry; imports only the contract from common.

metadata.label: limiter: address bans, lifts, promotions, the edge decisions read back, trap route touches, its own refusals (tallied) and the misbehaviour divisor (phase 55 01.6, 02.5, 02.6)

extensions.description: Phase 55 01.6: the actions the firewall's responder may take through this module (execute and undo call its own functions). Observe on install; the responder (05) owns modes, budgets and evidence.

metadata.label: limiter: ban an address, throttle an address (phase 55 01.6)

extensions.description: Phase 55 02.5: the trap routes: a few plausible old admin and backup API paths no module declares, so the dispatcher answers them with its own missing-route 404 and no sitemap or route listing can show them; the answer watcher reports a 404 on one as a critical signal (bounded per actor and per process).
